info.text: Midterm Discrete Mathematics exam (ACSP). 12 questions: Logic & predicates & inference (4), Discrete Structures (6), Proofs (2).

name.text: Q1 - Logical equivalence of a negated implication

questiontext.text: [Logic] Which proposition is logically equivalent to \( \neg(p \rightarrow q) \)?

generalfeedback.text: Since \( p ightarrow q \equiv eg p \lor q \), we get \( eg(p ightarrow q) \equiv eg( eg p \lor q) \equiv p \land eg q \) by De Morgan.

feedback.text: Correct — a true antecedent with a false consequent.
This is \(p \rightarrow q\) itself, not its negation.

questiontext.text: [Logic] The proposition \( \big(p \land (p \rightarrow q)\big) \rightarrow q \) is a tautology.

generalfeedback.text: True. This is exactly the Modus Ponens form; its truth table is true in every row.

feedback.text: Build the truth table: the implication holds in every case.

name.text: Q3 - Match each rule of inference to its form

questiontext.text: [Inference] Match each rule of inference with its symbolic form (premises \( \vdash \) conclusion).

generalfeedback.text: Modus Ponens: \(p,\; p o q \vdash q\). Modus Tollens: \( eg q,\; p o q \vdash eg p\). Hypothetical Syllogism: \(p o q,\; q o r \vdash p o r\). Disjunctive Syllogism: \(p\lor q,\; eg p \vdash q\).

incorrectfeedback.text: None correct — review the inference rules.

name.text: Q4 - Negation of a universally quantified implication

questiontext.text: [Predicates] What is the negation of \( \forall x\, \big(P(x) \rightarrow Q(x)\big) \)?

generalfeedback.text: \( eg orall x\,(P(x) o Q(x)) \equiv \exists x\, eg(P(x) o Q(x)) \equiv \exists x\,(P(x) \land eg Q(x)) \).

questiontext.text: [Sets] Let \(A\) and \(B\) be finite sets with \(|A| = 12\), \(|B| = 18\) and \(|A \cap B| = 5\). Compute \(|A \cup B|\).

name.text: Q6 - Set operations: De Morgan & cardinality (Cloze)

questiontext.text:
[Operations on Sets] Work in a universe \(U\) with \(|U| = 30\).

(a) By De Morgan's law, the complement of \(A \cup B\) equals {1:MULTICHOICE:=Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ~Aᶜ ∪ Bᶜ~A ∩ B~Aᶜ ∩ B}  (here Xᶜ denotes the complement of X).

(b) If \(|A| = 8\), then \( |\overline{A}| = \) {2:NUMERICAL:=22:0}.

(c) The number of subsets of a set with 4 elements is {1:NUMERICAL:=16:0}.

name.text: Q7 - Relations: properties of an equivalence relation

questiontext.text: [Relations] Define a relation \(R\) on \( \mathbb{Z} \) by \( a\,R\,b \iff a - b \text{ is even} \). Select all properties that \(R\) satisfies.

generalfeedback.text: \(a-a=0\) is even (reflexive); if \(a-b\) is even so is \(b-a\) (symmetric); if \(a-b\) and \(b-c\) are even, then \(a-c\) is even (transitive). So \(R\) is an equivalence relation — not antisymmetric (e.g. \(2R4\) and \(4R2\) with \(2\neq 4\)).

feedback.text: No — distinct congruent integers relate both ways.

questiontext.text: [Functions] Consider \( f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R},\ f(x)=2x+3 \). In one word, what kind of function is it (injective, surjective, or bijective — give the strongest correct term)?

generalfeedback.text: It is a non-constant affine map on \(\mathbb{R}\): one-to-one and onto, hence bijective. Its inverse is \( f^{-1}(y) = (y-3)/2 \).

name.text: Q9 - Sequences: term of a recurrence

questiontext.text: [Sequences] A sequence is defined by \( u_0 = 2 \) and \( u_{n+1} = 3u_n - 1 \) for \( n \ge 0 \). Compute \( u_3 \).

name.text: Q10 - Series: sum of an infinite geometric series

questiontext.text: [Series] Compute \( \displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{k} \). Give the answer as a decimal.

name.text: Q11 - Proof by contradiction: irrationality of sqrt(2)

questiontext.text: [Proof — Contradiction] Prove that \( \sqrt{2} \) is irrational using a proof by contradiction. State your assumption clearly, derive a contradiction, and conclude.

generalfeedback.text: Model proof. Assume, for contradiction, that \( \sqrt{2} \) is rational, so \( \sqrt{2} = \dfrac{a}{b} \) with \(a,b\in\mathbb{Z}\), \(b\neq 0\), and \( \gcd(a,b)=1 \). Then \( a^2 = 2b^2 \), so \(a^2\) is even, hence \(a\) is even: \(a = 2k\). Substituting, \(4k^2 = 2b^2 \Rightarrow b^2 = 2k^2\), so \(b\) is even too. Then \(2 \mid a\) and \(2 \mid b\), contradicting \( \gcd(a,b)=1 \). Therefore \( \sqrt{2} \) is irrational. \( \blacksquare \)

graderinfo.text: Award credit for: (1) stating the assumption \( \sqrt 2 = a/b \) in lowest terms; (2) deriving \(a\) even, then \(b\) even; (3) identifying the contradiction with \(\gcd(a,b)=1\); (4) correct conclusion.

name.text: Q12 - Proof by contraposition: n^2 even implies n even

questiontext.text: [Proof — Contraposition] Let \( n \in \mathbb{Z} \). Prove that if \( n^2 \) is even then \( n \) is even, using a proof by contraposition. State the contrapositive you will prove, then prove it.

generalfeedback.text: Model proof. The contrapositive is: "if \(n\) is odd then \(n^2\) is odd." Assume \(n\) is odd, so \(n = 2k+1\) for some \(k\in\mathbb{Z}\). Then \( n^2 = (2k+1)^2 = 4k^2 + 4k + 1 = 2(2k^2+2k) + 1 \), which is odd. Hence the contrapositive holds, and therefore the original statement "\(n^2\) even \(\Rightarrow n\) even" is true. \( \blacksquare \)

graderinfo.text: Award credit for: (1) correctly stating the contrapositive; (2) writing an odd \(n=2k+1\); (3) algebra showing \(n^2=2m+1\); (4) concluding the original implication.
